# Which relations completion offers columns of at the cursor (‸), checked by
# tests/scopes.rs through `completion::request`.
#
# Each case is a header line and the SQL after it:
#   == <dialect> | <relations> [| <columns>]
# <relations> are the relations of the cache whose columns are offered,
# comma-separated, written schema.table, or table for the tab's default
# schema; `none` when there are none, and `-` alone when the cursor asks for
# a relation name instead. <columns> are the columns the statement itself
# makes: those the SELECT list of a CTE or a derived table names (a `*` there
# offers the relations it reads, and a UNION names its columns by its first
# branch).
# After `alias.`: what the alias names (an outer alias from inside a
# subquery too). Otherwise: what the innermost query around the cursor reads
# (the statement, a subquery, a CTE body or a UNION branch). The test's index
# holds every relation the cases read, so one read in the wrong query shows.
#
# History: docs/investigacao-editor-sql.md, section G.4.

# Written for the tree-sitter proof of concept (64 cases).

== postgres | sales.orders
SELECT o.‸ FROM sales.orders o

== postgres | crm.customers
SELECT o.id, c.na‸ FROM sales.orders o JOIN crm.customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id

== postgres | orders
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE stat‸ = 'paid'

== postgres | customers
SELECT * FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.‸ = o.customer_id

== postgres | sales.orders
SELECT o.total::numeric(12,2), o.‸ FROM sales.orders AS o WHERE o.created_at >= now() - interval '7 days'

== postgres | crm.customers
WITH recent AS (SELECT customer_id FROM sales.orders WHERE created_at > now() - interval '1 day') SELECT c.‸ FROM recent r JOIN crm.customers c ON c.id = r.customer_id

== postgres | sales.orders
WITH recent AS (SELECT customer_id FROM sales.orders WHERE ‸ > now()) SELECT * FROM recent

== postgres | none | id, total
SELECT * FROM (SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE total > 0) big WHERE big.‸ > 10

== postgres | order_lines
SELECT o.id FROM orders o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_lines l WHERE l.‸ = o.id)

== postgres | orders
SELECT customer_id, sum(total) FROM orders GROUP BY cust‸ ORDER BY 2 DESC

== postgres | orders
SELECT customer_id, sum(total) AS spent FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY sp‸ DESC LIMIT 10

== postgres | sales.orders
UPDATE sales.orders AS o SET stat‸ = 'shipped' WHERE o.id = $1

== postgres | orders
DELETE FROM orders WHERE created_at < $1 AND stat‸ = 'cancelled'

== postgres | orders
SELECT DISTINCT ON (o.customer_id) o.‸ FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id ORDER BY o.customer_id, o.created_at DESC

== postgres | orders
SELECT o.id, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.‸) FROM orders o

== postgres | orders
SELECT o.data->>'sku', o.‸ FROM orders o WHERE o.data ? 'sku' AND o.note ILIKE '%gift%'

== postgres | customers
SELECT c.‸ FROM customers c LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT * FROM orders x WHERE x.customer_id = c.id LIMIT 1) last ON true

== postgres | "Sales"."Orders"
SELECT * FROM "Sales"."Orders" WHERE "Amo‸" > 0

== postgres | orders
SELECT o.‸ -- a comment with 'quotes' and ;
FROM orders o /* block /* nested */ comment */ WHERE o.note = 'it''s'

== postgres | events
SELECT e.‸ FROM events e WHERE e.payload = $$ {"a": "b;c"} $$

== postgres | orders
INSERT INTO archive.orders SELECT * FROM orders WHERE created_at < $1 AND ‸

== postgres | order_lines

== postgres | -
SELECT * FROM sales.ord‸ o

== postgres | sales.orders
SELECT o.total, 'São Paulo' AS cidade, o.‸ FROM sales.orders o

== mysql | shop.orders

== mysql | orders

== mysql | orders

== mysql | orders

== databricks | orders

== databricks | sales.orders

SELECT o.id FROM orders o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_lines l WHERE l.‸ = o.id)

# Written after its first results, for what those cases left out: an outer
# query over subqueries, CTEs and UNION branches, nested derived tables,
# correlated references, UPDATE … FROM, DELETE … USING, multi-table UPDATE
# and DELETE, INSERT column lists, MERGE with a subquery source (33 cases).

== postgres | orders
SELECT ‸ FROM orders o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_lines l WHERE l.order_id = o.id)

== postgres | crm.customers | customer_id
WITH r AS (SELECT customer_id FROM sales.orders) SELECT ‸ FROM r JOIN crm.customers c ON c.id = r.customer_id

== postgres | sales.orders
WITH r AS (SELECT customer_id FROM sales.orders WHERE ‸) SELECT * FROM r JOIN crm.customers c ON c.id = r.customer_id

== postgres | archive.orders
SELECT id FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT ‸ FROM archive.orders

== postgres | orders
SELECT ‸ FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT id FROM archive.orders

== postgres | none | id
SELECT t.‸ FROM (SELECT * FROM (SELECT id FROM orders) a) t

== postgres | customers
SELECT * FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.‸)

== postgres | staging.orders
UPDATE orders o SET total = s.total FROM staging.orders s WHERE o.id = s.‸

== postgres | customers
DELETE FROM orders o USING customers c WHERE o.customer_id = c.‸

== postgres | sales.orders
INSERT INTO sales.orders (id, ‸) VALUES (1, 2)

== postgres | orders,customers
SELECT ‸ FROM orders JOIN customers USING (customer_id)

== postgres | customers
SELECT c.‸ FROM orders o, customers c WHERE o.customer_id = c.id

== postgres | orders
SELECT o.id, (SELECT max(l.qty) FROM order_lines l WHERE l.order_id = o.id) AS top FROM orders o WHERE ‸

== postgres | customers
WITH a AS (SELECT * FROM orders), b AS (SELECT * FROM a JOIN customers c ON c.id = a.customer_id WHERE c.‸) SELECT * FROM b

== postgres | orders
SELECT "O".‸ FROM orders "O"

== postgres | sales.orders

== postgres | orders

== mysql | customers
UPDATE orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id SET o.status = 'x' WHERE c.‸ = 1

== mysql | orders

== mysql | orders,customers
INSERT INTO archive_orders SELECT ‸ FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id

== mysql | customers
SELECT id FROM orders UNION SELECT ‸ FROM customers

== mysql | orders
SELECT `my o`.‸ FROM orders `my o`

== mysql | customers

== mysql | orders

== databricks | crm.customers, sales.orders

== databricks | main.sales.orders

== databricks | sales.orders

== databricks | staging.orders

== databricks | crm.customers

== databricks | `main`.`sales`.`orders`

== databricks | sales.orders

# Written before the scope model was first run, with patterns used in
# neither set above (24 cases).

== postgres | orders,order_lines
SELECT ‸ FROM orders o LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT * FROM order_lines l WHERE l.order_id = o.id LIMIT 3) x ON true

== postgres | categories
WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (SELECT id, parent_id FROM categories WHERE parent_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.id, c.parent_id FROM categories c JOIN tree t ON c.‸ = t.id) SELECT * FROM tree

== postgres | none | id, name
SELECT ‸ FROM (SELECT o.id, c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id) AS t

== postgres | order_lines
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ANY (SELECT order_id FROM order_lines WHERE ‸)

== postgres | orders

== postgres | sales.orders

== postgres | orders
INSERT INTO audit (order_id, total) SELECT o.‸ FROM orders o WHERE o.total > 100 RETURNING id

== postgres | orders
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE ‸) FROM orders

== postgres | order_lines
DELETE FROM order_lines WHERE order_id IN (SELECT id FROM orders WHERE status = 'void') AND ‸

== postgres | hr.employees

== postgres | orders

== mysql | orders,customers
SELECT ‸ FROM orders o LEFT JOIN customers c USING (customer_id) WHERE o.total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM orders)

REPLACE INTO order_totals SELECT customer_id, SUM(‸) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id

== mysql | none | customer_id, last_order

== mysql | orders

== mysql | customers

== mysql | orders
INSERT INTO orders (customer_id, total) VALUES (1, 2) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE total = ‸

== databricks | sales.orders,crm.customers

== databricks | sales.orders
INSERT OVERWRITE sales.daily SELECT day, sum(‸) FROM sales.orders GROUP BY day

== databricks | sales.orders

== databricks | sales.keep

== databricks | sales.returns

# Reported by the maintainer: the columns of a CTE after its alias.

== postgres | none | num, email
with teste as (
  select nome as num,  email
  from sales.clientes
)
SELECT *
FROM type_showcase t
inner join sales.clientes c on c.id = t.id
inner join teste x on x.‸
WHERE t.id = 23 and t.flag = true;
